es.summary: Disminución de la temperatura central del cuerpo por debajo de 35 °C, que compromete la función metabólica y cardiovascular.
key_points: El frío y la humedad aumentan el riesgo.
La vasoconstricción reduce el flujo sanguíneo a órganos vitales.
Recalentamiento rápido previene arritmias y coagulopatía.

pathophysiology: El cuerpo pierde calor más rápido de lo que lo genera.
Se activa la vasoconstricción cutánea para conservar calor.
Disminuye la actividad enzimática y la producción de ATP.
La hipotermia profunda altera la conducción cardíaca y la coagulación.
risk_factors: Exposición prolongada al frío o al agua helada.
Consumo de alcohol o drogas que alteran la percepción del frío.
Enfermedades que disminuyen la termogénesis (hipotiroidismo, desnutrición).
signs_symptoms: Escalofríos, temblor, piel pálida y fría.
diagnostics: Monitorización continua de ECG y presión arterial.
Laboratorio: glucosa, electrolitos, gases arteriales (pH ↓, PaCO₂ ↑).
Evaluación de la piel para descartar congelación.
treatment: Retirar ropa mojada y cubrir al paciente con mantas térmicas.
Recalentamiento activo externo: bolsas de agua tibia, lámpara infrarroja.
Recalentamiento activo interno: sueros tibios (NS 37 °C), oxígeno humidificado caliente.
Monitoreo continuo de temperatura, ritmo cardíaco y presión arterial.
Administrar oxígeno suplementario si hay hipoxia.
nursing_care: Evaluar temperatura central cada 5‑15 min y registrar.
Mantener vía aérea permeable; aspirar secreciones si es necesario.
Aplicar fuentes de calor y verificar integridad cutánea.
Controlar signos vitales y ritmo cardíaco continuamente.
Documentar cambios en nivel de conciencia y perfusión periférica.
patient_teaching: Vestir varias capas de ropa seca y adecuada al clima.
Evitar alcohol y drogas antes de exponerse al frío.
Mantenerse activo y seco; buscar refugio al sentir temblores.
Reconocer signos tempranos de hipotermia y buscar ayuda inmediata.
En bebés, mantener la habitación a ≥20 °C y usar ropa adecuada.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de desequilibrio de la temperatura corporal
outcomes: Sin signos de temblor ni confusión

interventions.action: Evaluar temperatura central cada 5 min y registrar resultados.
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar rápidamente la caída de la temperatura y actuar a tiempo.

interventions.action: Retirar ropa mojada y cubrir al paciente con mantas térmicas o ropa seca.
interventions.rationale: Reduce la pérdida de calor y previene mayor descenso térmico.

interventions.action: Aplicar fuentes de calor activo (bolsas de agua tibia, lámpara infrarroja).
interventions.rationale: Acelera el recalentamiento del cuerpo de forma controlada.

interventions.action: Administrar líquidos tibios por vía intravenosa según indicación médica.
interventions.rationale: Contribuye al recalentamiento interno y evita hipotermia secundaria.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente y familia sobre vestimenta adecuada y riesgos del alcohol.
interventions.rationale: Previene recurrencias al modificar conductas de riesgo.

en.summary: A decrease in the body's core temperature below 35 °C, compromising metabolic and cardiovascular function.
key_points: Cutaneous vasoconstriction reduces blood flow to vital organs.
Rapid rewarming prevents arrhythmias and coagulopathy.

pathophysiology: The body loses heat faster than it generates it.
Cutaneous vasoconstriction is activated to conserve heat.
Enzymatic activity and ATP production decrease.
Deep hypothermia alters cardiac conduction and coagulation.
risk_factors: Prolonged exposure to cold or icy water.
Alcohol or drug use that alters cold perception.
signs_symptoms: Shivering, tremor, pale and cold skin.
diagnostics: Continuous ECG and blood pressure monitoring.
Skin assessment to rule out frostbite.
treatment: Remove wet clothing and cover the patient with thermal blankets.
Active external rewarming: warm water bags, infrared lamp.
Active internal rewarming: warm fluids (NS 37 °C), heated humidified oxygen.
Continuous monitoring of temperature, heart rhythm, and blood pressure.
Administer supplemental oxygen if hypoxia is present.
nursing_care: Assess core temperature every 5‑15 min and record.
Maintain a patent airway; suction secretions if necessary.
Apply heat sources and check skin integrity.
Continuously monitor vital signs and heart rhythm.
Document changes in level of consciousness and peripheral perfusion.
patient_teaching: Wear multiple layers of dry, weather-appropriate clothing.
Avoid alcohol and drugs before cold exposure.
Stay active and dry; seek shelter when shivering begins.
Recognize early signs of hypothermia and seek immediate help.
In infants, keep the room at ≥20 °C and use appropriate clothing.

outcomes: No signs of shivering or confusion

interventions.action: Assess core temperature every 5 min and record results.
interventions.rationale: Allows rapid detection of temperature drop and timely action.

interventions.action: Remove wet clothing and cover the patient with thermal blankets or dry clothing.
interventions.rationale: Reduces heat loss and prevents further cooling.

interventions.action: Apply active heat sources (warm water bags, infrared lamp).
interventions.rationale: Accelerates controlled rewarming of the body.

interventions.action: Administer warm intravenous fluids as ordered by the physician.
interventions.rationale: Contributes to internal rewarming and prevents secondary hypothermia.

interventions.action: Educate the patient and family about appropriate clothing and alcohol risks.
interventions.rationale: Prevents recurrences by modifying risk behaviors.

sources.name: Fundamentals of Nursing: Safety: Individual and Environmental

summary.0.quote: Hypothermia A drop in core body temperature below 96.8°F (36°C), or hypothermia, can have significant consequences during surgery and potentially affect patient outcomes.

key_points.0.quote: A body temperature below 95 °F (35 °C) is a medical emergency and can lead to death if not treated promptly.

key_points.2.quote: In an attempt to conserve heat, the body constricts blood vessels, reducing blood flow to vital organs.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: A condition that occurs when the body loses heat faster than it can produce it is called hypothermia.

sections.pathophysiology.1.quote: In an attempt to conserve heat, the body constricts blood vessels, reducing blood flow to vital organs.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: You can also get it from being cold and wet, or under cold water for too long.

sections.risk_factors.3.quote: For example, a person who is impaired by either alcohol or drugs may choose to go outside when the weather is extremely cold and may not recognize how cold it is, perhaps losing consciousness or falling asleep in the cold, leading to hypothermia.

sections.risk_factors.4.quote: Underlying medical conditions: Patients with preexisting conditions like thyroid disorders or malnutrition may be more susceptible to hypothermia.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: A body temperature below 95 °F (35 °C) is a medical emergency and can lead to death if not treated promptly.

sections.complications.4.quote: Cardiac arrest is sudden cessation of heartbeat and cardiac function, caused by an electrical disturbance or a lethal rhythm resulting in the loss of effective circulation.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Avoid alcohol and drugs, as they can impair judgment and increase the risk of hypothermia.
